question: What will the September 2026 ISM Manufacturing PMI be?

calls.reasoning: Status quo is 54.6 (August), and for a diffusion index the prior print is the single best one-month predictor; the reference class of monthly ISM changes is centered near zero with SD approx 1.3. I shade slightly below status quo for three reasons: New Orders decelerated 3 points to 53.7 with backlogs weakening (forward driver of the composite), both September regional surveys already in hand moderated hard (Empire 20.6 -> 7.6; Philly 47.4 -> 37.8, employment 27.9 -> 11.8), and readings above 54 historically carry mild negative drift. Offsetting and keeping me close to status quo: Production is still 58.3, both regional levels remain well above zero in absolute terms, and worsening supply availability / substantially lengthening delivery times mechanically inflate the PMI through the inverted supplier-deliveries component. Macro backdrop is two-sided: an energy shock (Brent approx $96, +42% y/y on renewed US-Iran strikes) and a possible Fed hike are demand negatives, while eight months of expansion have persisted through exactly that. Market check: Polymarket's bracket ladder matches this question's source, release date and headline-figure definition, and implies a mean near 54.3 with an SD around 1.5 on thin volume (594-4,924); Kalshi KXISMPMI-26SEP exists but the page returned 429/403 so I recorded no price; no Manifold or bookmaker market found. Trading Economics projects 54.0 at quarter end. The September S&P Global flash (9/23) would be the biggest missing input and lands after this run, so my dispersion stays at the full reference-class width rather than tightening.

calls.reconciliation: Disputes were mostly about magnitude, not fact. (1) Energy-shock provenance (US-Iran strikes vs Red Sea/Yanbu disruption) could not be settled without web access; both are same-signed cost shocks already embedded in prior prints, so the median does not turn on it. (2) Dispersion: I rejected the 2026-only SD of ~1.1 as a 10-observation artifact and used the 2015-2026 ex-COVID SD of ~1.33, giving a 10-90 width of 3.4. (3) Conditional drift: I weighted the above-54 mean-reversion term (-0.3) over the 2026 regime drift (+0.1) because the conditioning variable is already known. (4) The runs quoted three different market centers (54.0, 54.2, 54.3); I recomputed the bracket-midpoint mean from the harness-supplied prices myself and got 54.18 on the six visible brackets, with a near-symmetric 53-53.9/55-55.9 pair and a mild left skew from the 51-51.9 bucket - so ~54.1-54.4 is the honest read and the low-end fat tails are overround on sub-$400 buckets. (5) Whether the sharp Empire/Philly declines or their still-elevated levels dominate is pure judgment with no tiebreaker in the dossiers; I took the partial shade I would bet on rather than the full change-regression implication of -0.6 to -0.9. Net effect: I sit 0.1 above the runs' cluster, which is where the reconciled evidence lands once the no-serial-continuation point and the supplier-deliveries mechanic are given their weight. I carried forward Run 3's reference class, which I agree with.
